papers.title: The stability of non-Abelian $A_4$ vortices in $SO(3)$ gauge theory
papers.abstract: We study the linear energetic stability of non-Abelian vortices in an $SO(3)$ gauge-Higgs theory with residual gauge group $A_4$. In our previous work, we identified two families of such vortices associated with order-two and order-three elements of $A_4$, and found Bogomol'nyi--Prasad--Sommerfield-like behavior at special ratios of the Higgs and gauge-boson mass scales. Here, we investigate their stability against $SO(3)$ gauge and Higgs perturbations by analyzing the second order variation of the vortex tension using analytical and numerical methods. In particular, when all relevant mass scales are equal, we prove linear stability for all vortices in the order-three family. By contrast, at the same mass point, we prove that a vortex in the order-two family is unstable. Thus, although both vortex families exhibit Bogomol'nyi--Prasad--Sommerfield-like behavior in their reduced equations at this mass point, their stability properties in the full $SO(3)$ theory are qualitatively different.

papers.title: MoEDAL-MAPP: the first dedicated search experiment at the LHC
papers.abstract: This special issue brings together a collection of original research articles and review papers addressing topics directly related to the MoEDAL-MAPP experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The experiment is designed to search for (meta-)stable, anomalously ionising particles predicted by theoretical extensions of the Standard Model. Several contributions explore the theoretical and phenomenological aspects of models of particular relevance to the experiment, including scenarios involving magnetic monopoles, highly electrically charged particles, and millicharged particles. Other contributions focus on experimental developments, highlighting novel detection techniques and technological advances aimed at identifying these unconventional signatures and probing new phenomena beyond the Standard Model.

papers.title: The Semileptonic B Frontier: LHC, B-factories, Lattice QCD & the Hunt for Precision
papers.abstract: This review document summarizes the main outcomes and key theoretical and experimental developments discussed at the workshop ``The Semileptonic $B$ Frontier: LHC, $B$-Factories, Lattice QCD & the Hunt for Precision'', held at Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati on 16--18 February, https://agenda.infn.it/event/49469/. Bringing together experimentalists and theorists, the meeting addressed recent advances and outstanding challenges in both charged-current ($b \to c/u\,\ellν$) and neutral-current ($b \to s\,\ell^+\ell^-$) semileptonic $b$-hadron decays. We synthesize current experimental measurements from Belle, Belle~II, and LHCb with state-of-the-art theoretical inputs---including Lattice QCD determinations, Heavy Quark Expansion (HQE) frameworks, and QED radiative corrections. In addition to reviewing the status of CKM matrix elements, hadronic form factor extractions, and Lepton Flavor Universality (LFU) tests, this report highlights novel observables and fitting techniques designed to maximize the sensitivity of future analyses and guide upcoming data-taking campaigns.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced Search for Galactic Dark Photons Using Cat-State Cavities
papers.abstract: We present a quantum-enhanced search for the Galactic dark-photon background (GDPB), a relativistic and anisotropic vector field that can be produced by dark-matter decay or annihilation in the Milky Way halo. We reinterpret an existing quantum-enhanced dark-photon dataset obtained with a superconducting circuit QED platform originally developed for wave-like dark-photon dark-matter searches, consisting of a high-$Q$ niobium cavity in the $\mathrm{TM}_{010}$ mode dispersively coupled to a transmon qubit. By preparing four-component cat states and performing repeated quantum non-demolition parity measurements, analyzed with a hidden Markov model, we extract photon-transition probabilities for multiple cat amplitudes and integration times. The coupling to the GDPB is governed by a polarization- and angle-dependent cavity overlap function, which predicts a distinctive diurnal modulation of the excitation rate for both longitudinal and transverse polarizations. From the absence of such modulation, we set 90\% confidence-level bounds on the kinetic-mixing parameter $ε$ for two benchmark production mechanisms (parametric and cascade decay) over the relativistic mass range $m_X \ll ω_c$.

papers.title: Decoherence as a Detector-Resolution Flow
papers.abstract: We consider the QED final-state radiation modeled by $γγ^\ast\toπ^+π^-+X$, including its finite-temperature generalization, as an open quantum system, and study the evolution of the pion-pair momentum density matrix as the detector resolution scale is varied. We derive an explicit relation between the Lindblad jump operator and the Wilson line associated with soft photon radiation. We find that real emission and virtual correction serve as two separate contributions to momentum decoherence, and together they give rise to the real--virtual cancellation at the density-matrix level. The external finite-temperature photon bath modifies the decoherence rate by a Bose factor consistent with the Feynman--Vernon influence-functional approach. We emphasize that our conclusions also apply to hard fermion production thanks to the universality of the soft radiation.

papers.title: Superhorizon enhancement of the hydrodynamic GW tail in Standard Model embedded warm inflation
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamic fluctuations in the primordial plasma generate a gravitational-wave (GW) background that grows like $f^3_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ in terms of the current frequency. However, within the ($10^{-4}_{ } ... 10^4_{ })\,$Hz band of upcoming interferometers, the modes likely re-entered the Hubble horizon when the hydrodynamic noise was no longer at its maximal value. To address this situation, we define a model-independent transfer function for GWs generated by hydrodynamic (or other white-noise) fluctuations at any time. Employing appropriate variables, we show how this transfer function, together with the simpler vacuum one, can be determined numerically for a general expansion history. The results are illustrated for Standard Model embedded warm inflation scenarios, including both the vacuum and hydrodynamic parts. Following previous estimates, we find that a pre-exit-generated hydrodynamic tail becomes almost flat below $(10^5_{ } ... 10^7_{ })\;$Hz. Its small-$f^{ }_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ intercept remains finite, and can then moderately influence observational constraints through the tensor-to-scalar ratio ($r$).

papers.title: Thermal spectral functions of heavy and exotic Mesons from a hQCD at finite density
papers.abstract: In this work, we study spectral functions of heavy and exotic mesons in a self-consistent Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton model at finite temperature and chemical potential, where the dilaton is allowed to back-react on the geometry. A non-quadratic dilaton profile is introduced to reproduce the nonlinear Regge trajectories of heavy-flavor mesons, and the corresponding spectral functions are computed for charmonium, bottomonium, tetraquark, and hybrid channels. In all cases, increasing either temperature or chemical potential suppresses and broadens the quasiparticle peaks, signaling sequential in-medium dissociation; for each radial family, the 2S-like state melts before the 1S-like state. The predicted melting temperatures obey the mass ordering $T_{\rm melt}^{π_1(1400)}<T_{\rm melt}^{J/ψ}<T_{\rm melt}^{Z_c(3900)}<T_{\rm melt}^{Υ(1S)}$, with $T_{\rm melt}\simeq 1.08,\ 2.96,\ 4.44$, and $5.93\,T_c$, respectively, so heavier states remain bound up to higher temperatures. These results provide quantitative, testable predictions for heavy-ion experiments probing tetraquark and hybrid mesons in hot and dense QCD matter.

papers.title: Binding energies in the $0^{-+}$ and $1^{--}$ fermion--antifermion channels from the ladder Bethe-Salpeter and Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract: In this work, we calculate the binding energies of an equal-mass fermion--antifermion system in the $0^{-+}$ and $1^{--}$ channels from the ladder Bethe--Salpeter (BS) equation with scalar, pseudoscalar, and vector exchange. The results are compared with those of the Schrödinger equation with the corresponding leading static interaction in two regimes: pointlike massless exchange at weak coupling and finite-mass exchange with monopole form factors at stronger coupling. For the BS calculation, we use two independent numerical methods based on momentum-space integral equations and coordinate-space differential equations. The differential-equation method gives estimated relative binding-energy errors below $10^{-9}$ in both regimes. For massless vector exchange in Coulomb gauge, the numerical results are consistent with the uncrossed-ladder perturbative spectrum through the $O(mα^5)$ terms. The results for massless scalar exchange and vector exchange in Feynman gauge are consistent with the common Wick--Cutkosky expansion through order $mα^3$. For finite exchange masses, the differences from the leading static Schrödinger spectra at the same masses, couplings, and form factors depend strongly on the exchange and channel. Scalar exchange gives nearly degenerate channels with much weaker binding than the Schrödinger reference. In contrast, vector exchange with only the metric term retained gives stronger binding than the Schrödinger reference in $0^{-+}$ and weaker binding in $1^{--}$. Notably, retaining the full Proca numerator substantially increases the vector binding in both channels. Pseudoscalar exchange also supports bound states and favors $1^{--}$, although its leading static central interaction vanishes.

papers.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
papers.abstract: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.

papers.title: Constraints on pion parton distributions at small $x$ from leading-neutron electroproduction data
papers.abstract: We revisit the extraction of parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the pion in a global QCD analysis of pion--nucleus Drell--Yan and leading-neutron (LN) electroproduction data, in view of recent suggestions that uncertainties on the pion PDFs at small parton momentum fraction $x$ are dramatically underestimated. We perform a set of controlled fits that vary the LN data coverage, PDF parametrization, and positivity constraints, determining both the PDFs and pion-nucleon splitting functions simultaneously. While the use of a restricted H1 LN data sample used by the Fantômas group is found to enlarge the PDF uncertainties and admit solutions with vanishing gluon PDFs, our global analysis provides a good description of an extended H1 and ZEUS LN database, significantly reducing the parametrization dependence and strongly disfavoring a zero gluon distribution.
